assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only mass-effect:commander-shepard@renegade-player-archetype#renegade-shepard-monograph, the canonical interpretive monograph MASS_EFFECT_RENEGADE_SHEPARD_CHARACTER_MONOGRAPH.md at basis_commit, read in full. It is the study's analytical-corpus formulation of a player archetype extracted from the trilogy's choice space, and it declares itself not an exhaustive transcript audit. The study's corpus map and the Paragon monograph were consulted for scope and provenance only and are not evidence on this subject. No game transcript, mission dialogue, audiovisual recording, specific playthrough, novel, comic or external documentation is included, and the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The whole Mass Effect trilogy as three coarse phases (ME1 hard-edged human instrument, ME2 mission-first operator inside Cerberus, ME3 emergency sovereign) through the ending choice. No mission-level or in-game chronology, no particular playthrough state, and no pre-trilogy or post-ending state is established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph states a ranked value hierarchy under existential conditions (survival, neutralizing the threat, mission, loyalty, deterrence, then law, transparency, mercy and legitimacy where compatible), a central fear of losing through unwillingness to become hard enough, a reflexive test against manufactured necessity, nine failure modes, five internal subtypes, twelve simulation defaults, and lists of arguments that persuade, provoke or change the archetype's mind (sections 4, 16, 51-59, 66-70, 88-91). That supports interpretation of what the archetype values, fears and refuses. These rules are analyst-constructed and located in no game scene, and the monograph leaves decisive variables open: whether self-awareness succeeds (88.11), which subtype is in play, and the Destroy/Control split. So it gives no determinate behavioral model.

Three game-level phases are characterized as thematic stances: hard-edged human instrument (ME1), mission-first operator in contaminated space (ME2), emergency sovereign (ME3) (sections 35-37). There is no within-game ordering, mission sequence or state-transition rule.

Communicative tendencies are described at the analyst level: impatience with evasion, controlled anger, an edge to humor, willingness to threaten, care shown by solving the danger rather than narrating care, and grief that is compartmentalized (sections 32-34). No game dialogue is quoted or analyzed, and the block-quoted lines are explicitly 'analytical shorthand' (section 35). This answers only bounded questions about the archetype's stated affect. It is not a source-supported voice, and it says nothing about the games' actual dialogue.
The monograph contains no ordinary, off-duty or low-stakes behavior, so nothing is established. Its loyalty to the crew (section 26) is a command stance, not mundane conduct.

Stances are given by category: squadmates and crew ('hard outside, loyal inside', sections 26-27), romantic partners only under a consent boundary (section 28), enemies judged by threat status who can become allies without being forgiven (sections 20-22), alien species within Alliance patriotism and an anti-supremacist boundary (sections 23-25), and Council, Cerberus and the Illusive Man as institutions or ideological mirrors (sections 14, 29-31). No individual squadmate or romance partner is named, so only category-level canon questions are supported.

The analyst attributes stated beliefs and fears to the archetype: the fear of losing for lack of hardness, self-suspicion about needing things to be necessary, compartmentalized grief, guilt that does not prove wrongness, and the risk of moral numbness (sections 5, 16, 32, 58, 72). They support bounded questions about the archetype's professed stance. They are not depicted interior states of a specific Shepard.

A force doctrine is stated: credible rather than maximal violence, fear directed at threats and not at the crew, a preemption threshold that rises with the severity of harm, enemies triaged by whether they can still do harm, functional anger rather than rage, and no spending of lives to prove toughness (sections 8, 10-12, 20-22, 33). This is a doctrine, not located conflict behavior. The Collector Base and other trilogy decisions are discussed as tensions, and none is shown in a scene.

The core is a dirty-hands, survival-first ethic. It includes explicit deliberation questions for civilian harm, including the test of whether the archetype would accept the same logic if the victims were human or personally known (section 18). It distinguishes real emergency from ordinary danger or inconvenience (section 13), and it works through all four endings with a ranked preference (sections 38-42). This identifies the considerations the archetype weighs. The deliberation is the analyst's reconstruction, located in no game text, and the monograph leaves the decisive Destroy/Control divide open.

Humor is characterized in one passage, as dark and edged, belittling pompous authority or threatening indirectly (sections 32 and 34). No instance is given. It supports only the bounded question of whether, and in what key, the archetype uses humor.

The front matter and section 0 declare the monograph a corpus-governing interpretive model, not an exhaustive transcript audit. It cites no missions, dialogue lines, codex entries or recordings and names no edition or playthrough. The breadth is trilogy-wide but unlocated in the source.

Affirmative limits are stated. The archetype is not 'evil Shepard', not sadism, not random aggression, not automatic xenophobia, not Cerberus Shepard, not pure utilitarian arithmetic, and not every red option. Some Renegade-tagged game choices are named as incompatible with the archetype (sections 0, 60-65). There is an explicit anti-supremacist boundary (section 24) and a rule that extreme configurations must be qualified (section XXIV). These counter a flattening villain reading, but as interpretive assertions rather than located contradictions.
Only the three-game phase structure and the ending choice are placed in time. No default state is fixed when a period is unspecified, and no mission or date chronology is supplied.

scenario_readiness.note: The monograph contains no attested dialogue, and its quotations are analytical shorthand (section 35). Dialogue generated from its affect profile or its persuasion and provocation lists would be fluent invention, not source-supported voice. This bounds the evidence set, not the games.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The trilogy-wide corpus archetype at any of its three coarse phases; no mission-level moment or playthrough state is fixed.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Any counterpart, since the monograph names no individual relationship; the refusal holds for crew, allies, enemies, institutions and comparison characters alike.
setting_constraints: Crossover, counterfactual or materially novel contexts outside the trilogy's command situations, including the monograph's own comparative pairings
Behavioral or dialogue simulation rather than analyst-level value comparison
No fixed personality, located scene evidence or decision procedure is available in this evidence set, and the disciplined-versus-failure-state variable is unresolved

scenario_readiness.note: Section 88 offers 'default assumptions when simulating', and sections 82-87 anchor comparisons with Reinhard, Oberstein, the Illusive Man, Sung Jinwoo and Yang Wen-li. These are the project's own use guidance for analyst-level value comparison, not evidence of behavioral sufficiency. The monograph disclaims a fixed personality, leaves whether self-awareness succeeds as 'a major variable', and supplies no located behavior, speech or decision procedure. Cross-scenario simulation is therefore not supported by this evidence set. The scope names the only context in which even this refusal was assessed.
No ordinary social content; nothing is established.

conditions: The dilemma is a command-context ethical or political choice of the kind the monograph treats: existential threat, use of force and fear, preemption, civilian triage, mercy toward dangerous actors, secrecy, emergency authority, use of Cerberus-like resources.

Output is a value-level account of what the archetype weighs and refuses, stated as tendency rather than certainty, with the section 51-59 failure modes and the section 16 self-suspicion test available as counterweights.
Where the monograph leaves a choice open (Destroy versus Control, which subtype is in play, whether self-awareness succeeds), the alternatives are stated rather than resolved.

The subject is the unqualified disciplined archetype of the corpus-use rule, not any particular player's Shepard or an extreme configuration, and no specific mission mechanics, dialogue lines, squadmate names or playthrough facts are asserted as canon.
scenario_readiness.note: The civilian-harm questions, the emergency distinctions and the ending doctrine model this kind of reasoning. Readiness is conditional because the doctrine is interpretive, located in no game text, and leaves its decisive divide open.

Romance appears only as principle: private attachment, including to romantic partners, is compatible with the archetype, and coercive sexuality or romantic entitlement is not (sections 26 and 28). No partner, relationship history or intimate conduct is given, so the evidence set affirmatively falls short of supporting relationship behavior.

conditions: Military-professional command or political-military context framed by the Alliance, N7 and Spectre foundation the monograph describes (sections 1-3).

Prediction is limited to command posture and priorities: tempo as an ethical variable, responsibility for outcomes, credible deterrence, owning sacrifice, hostility to bureaucratic evasion, and trust in competent persons over slow procedure. It does not extend to tactics, procedure or speech.
No specific mission, squad composition or in-game outcome is asserted.
The failure modes (intimidation addiction, emergency becoming permanent, control as an end) remain possible outcomes and are not excluded.
scenario_readiness.note: The monograph's subject is military command under existential pressure, so prediction of posture is supported. Operational detail is not.

known_limits.statement: Section 0 states that the games provide a player-directed range of Renegade-tagged actions, some mutually inconsistent, and that the monograph selects a coherent through-line instead of claiming a fixed personality. Every claim here concerns the corpus archetype, not a canonical individual.

Sections 0 and 60-65 state that Renegade Shepard is not 'evil Shepard', sadism, random aggression, automatic xenophobia, Cerberus Shepard, pure utilitarian arithmetic or every red option, and that some Renegade-tagged choices fall outside the archetype.

The front matter and section 0 declare the monograph a corpus-governing interpretive model, not an exhaustive transcript audit. Its block quotations are analytical shorthand (section 35), and the trilogy decisions it names are discussed without scene evidence.

The monograph leaves the archetype's decisive variables unresolved. Whether its self-awareness succeeds is 'a major variable' (section 88, item 11). The Destroy/Control split is its 'central late-stage divide' (section 42). The five subtypes are emphases within it, not settled states (section 66 onward). Predictions that settle these points are unsupported.

The corpus-use rule (section XXIV) restricts the unqualified name to the disciplined military-professional archetype. Extreme configurations such as a control-aligned or supremacist Shepard must be named explicitly and are not assessed here.

This evidence set contains no attested dialogue or register, no individual squadmate or romance relationship, no mundane behavior, no mission chronology, and no edition or playthrough variable (origin, class, gender, survivors). Missing support is not evidence that the games lack them.
